newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK October producer price data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK October producer price data.

text.p: Following is a selection of economists' reactions to UK producer price data showing October input prices up 0.5 pct s/adj month-on-month and down 2.0 pct yr/yr, output prices up unadj 0.2 pct m/m and up 2.3 pct yr/yr:

"Input prices were a bit higher than we expected. Two things to note -- it is an erratic figure and the fact it's down 2.0 percent on the year is still in absolute terms a good result, and also it's being driven by petroleum prices rather than other commodity prices."

"On the output side, fairly reasonable, although even there the headline number was a little above what most analysts were looking for. The input price side is a little surprising -- we had expected the rise in sterling to have dampened the oil price effect. By the time we get to next month's figures, I think the worst of the oil price rise will have come through and we'll be seeing the positive effects from the rise in sterling."

"Minimal 0.1 pct gain in UK core output prices should give a little help to a financial market clearly worried about another rate hike before the election. The annual rate in this index remained at just 0.9 pct last month, its lowest increase since 1967 and far enough below the RPIX to imply no obvious threat to the government's inflation target. Data of no immediate implications for Thursday's RPIs but are nonetheless consistent with those surveys that continue to indicate highly competitive conditions precluding any significant hike in rates."

"(Input prices) It's mildly disappointing and I think it does point to slightly stronger price pressures coming through the production process. I agree that maybe they won't be sustained but that does require continued sterling appreciation. The output side figures are pretty good too. I think there will be a mild amount of disappointment, but nothing serious, on the back of these data."
